data.title: Linamar to Acquire Terex's Aerials Unit for $1.4B
data.description:
By Katherine Hamilton

Linamar will acquire Terex's aerials business, including the well-known Genie brand, for $1.4 billion in cash.

The business unit designs and manufactures lifts, telehandlers and elevated work platforms. The deal, which is expected to close in the first half, includes all assets, intellectual property and manufacturing sites under the unit.

The Canadian manufacturing firm said Monday the business will be added to its industrial segment, joining its lifts brand Skyjack. The brands will continue to operate separately, but Linamar expects the deal to eventually lead to savings of about $135 million a year.

Linamar also expects Genie will add about $2.3 billion of revenue on a last 12-months basis to segment revenue. The deal is being financed through a new credit facility with National Bank of Canada.

Terex, also a manufacturer, said the deal was part of its efforts to transform its business. The exited its tower and rough terrain cranes business in 2025, and acquired an environmental solutions unit in 2024. After the sale is completed the company will have three operating segments: environmental solutions, materials processing and specialty vehicles.

Proceeds from the deal to reduce net debt, return capital and support growth investments, Terex said.

Write to Katherine Hamilton at katherine.hamilton@wsj.com

data.title: ADENTRA to Acquire AccessSMT, a Leading Canadian Distributor of Commercial Doors, Hardware and Access Control Products, for C$230 Million
data.description:
Acquisition expands ADENTRA's Canadian commercial presence, strengthens its doors and value-added services offering and is expected to deliver 10% to 15% Adjusted basic EPS accretion

  • The acquisition builds on ADENTRA's established doors category in the U.S. and commercial business. On a pro forma basis, the commercial business is expected to increase from approximately 13% to approximately 18% of ADENTRA's total sales, while Canadian sales are expected to approximately double, representing 14% of total sales.
  • AccessSMT is expected to generate sales of approximately C$240 million (US$172 million) in 2026. On a pro forma annualized basis, the acquisition is expected to increase ADENTRA's 2026 Adjusted basic EPS by 10% to 15%, and be accretive to both gross margin and Adjusted EBITDA margin.
  • The acquisition will be funded through ADENTRA's existing revolving credit facility. Pro Forma Leverage Ratio is expected to be approximately 3.0x at closing, compared with 2.3x as at September 30, 2026.
  • Closing is expected in December 2026, subject to customary conditions, including Competition Act approval.

LANGLEY, BC, Nov. 23, 2026 /CNW/ -- ADENTRA Inc. ("ADENTRA" or the "Company") () today announced that it has, through a wholly-owned subsidiary, entered into a definitive stock purchase agreement (the "Purchase Agreement") to acquire (the "Acquisition") all of the issued and outstanding shares of AccessSMT Holdings Ltd. (together with its subsidiaries, "AccessSMT"), a leading Canadian distributor of commercial doors, frames, hardware, and access controls, for C$230 million (approximately US$164 million), subject to customary adjustments (the "Purchase Price"). AccessSMT brings an established market position, attractive margins, a substantial contracted backlog and opportunities for continued growth.

"AccessSMT combines a leading market position, long-standing customer relationships and a value-added service offering that supports attractive margins," said Rob Brown, ADENTRA's President and CEO. "Doors are an established product category for our U.S. business, and the Acquisition significantly expands our presence in the Canadian commercial market, including healthcare, institutional and other commercial end markets. We are pleased to welcome Mike Barnes, who will continue to lead AccessSMT, and his experienced team to ADENTRA."

"We expect the Acquisition to deliver 10% to 15% Adjusted basic EPS accretion, while maintaining a Pro Forma Leverage Ratio of approximately 3.0x at closing," continued Mr. Brown. "This is our eighteenth acquisition since 2010, our fourth scale acquisition since 2021, and remains consistent with the capital deployment priorities of our Long-Term Value Creation Framework1. Our focus on maintaining a well-capitalized balance sheet enables us to fund the Acquisition within our existing credit facility."

"Joining ADENTRA provides AccessSMT with a long-term partner and the resources to support our continued growth," said Mike Barnes, AccessSMT's Chief Executive Officer. "Our customers and suppliers will continue to work with the same people, at the same locations and receive the same service and support they rely on today. Our team will also benefit from being part of one of North America's largest distributors of architectural building products."

Acquisition Highlights

A scaled national leader with long-standing customer relationships. AccessSMT is a leading distributor of commercial doors and related products in Canada, with a national platform of 15 locations across six provinces and Washington State. Its offering spans doors, frames and hardware, access control and specialty building products, allowing customers to source a project's complete openings package from a single provider. AccessSMT serves approximately 4,500 customers, many on a repeat basis.

  • ______________________________

  • 1 For more information on the Long-Term Value Creation Framework, see the investor presentation on the Company's website

An attractive, growing market. Canada's commercial door market is expected to grow at a compound annual rate of approximately 4.9% through 2030, supported by non-residential and multi-family construction, replacement and retrofit activity, evolving building code requirements and increasing demand for pre-assembled door systems that improve installation efficiency and reduce on-site labour requirements (see "Third-Party Information" below).

A differentiated model built around value-added services. AccessSMT supports customers from design and specification through fabrication, pre-assembly, delivery, installation and ongoing service and maintenance. This integrated offering reduces on-site labour requirements, simplifies project coordination and enables timely project delivery, while contributing to AccessSMT's attractive margins.

Contracted backlog and retrofit activity support business quality. At October 31, 2026, AccessSMT's contracted backlog exceeded its revenue for the preceding twelve months, providing visibility into future activity. The backlog includes major healthcare and institutional projects across Canada, further expanding ADENTRA's exposure to these end markets. Approximately 70% of AccessSMT's jobs involve upgrades and retrofits to existing buildings, complementing demand from new construction.

A platform for continued growth. AccessSMT has opportunities to expand its geographic footprint, service capabilities and product offering. The Canadian commercial door distribution market also remains fragmented, with more than 100 smaller local and regional distributors accounting for approximately half of the market. ADENTRA can support AccessSMT's growth opportunities through capital, operating expertise and shared resources.

Financial Overview and Transaction Terms

ADENTRA has agreed to acquire all the issued and outstanding shares of AccessSMT from Speyside CAN Holdings, LLC, a portfolio company of Speyside Equity Fund I (the "Seller"), for the Purchase Price, which includes customary adjustments for cash, indebtedness, transaction expenses and net working capital relative to an agreed target. The Purchase Price is payable in cash at closing, with no deferred or contingent consideration.

ADENTRA will fund the Purchase Price through borrowings under its existing senior secured credit facility with Bank of America, N.A. and a syndicate of lenders, which includes a revolving credit facility of up to US$600 million. As at September 30, 2026, ADENTRA had approximately US$453 million of undrawn capacity under the revolving credit facility. No new financing commitment or equity issuance is required to complete the Acquisition.

In connection with the Acquisition, members of AccessSMT management have agreed to subscribe for common shares of ADENTRA for aggregate proceeds of approximately C$2 million at a price per share equal to the five-day volume-weighted average trading price of ADENTRA's common shares on the Toronto Stock Exchange (the "TSX") immediately prior to the closing of the Acquisition. The subscription is subject to the approval of the TSX. The shares will be subject to a statutory four-month hold period.

Completion of the Acquisition is subject to customary closing conditions for a transaction of this nature, including the receipt of approval under the Competition Act (Canada). The Purchase Agreement contains termination provisions customary for a transaction of this nature, including a right of either party to terminate if, subject to certain conditions, closing has not occurred by December 31, 2026, at which date ADENTRA may extend by up to 60 days if approval under the Competition Act (Canada) is outstanding. The Acquisition is expected to close in December 2026, following receipt of approval under the Competition Act (Canada).

About AccessSMT

Headquartered in Vancouver, British Columbia, AccessSMT Holdings Ltd. is a leading Canadian distributor of commercial doors, frames and hardware, access control and specialty building products, with roots dating back to 1928. AccessSMT provides an end-to-end solution, including design, fabrication, pre-assembly, installation, and service and maintenance, for critical infrastructure, institutional, healthcare, education, commercial and multi-family residential projects. AccessSMT employs approximately 490 people at 15 locations across six Canadian provinces and Washington State. Its operating subsidiaries include CP Distributors Ltd., McGregor Hardware Distributors Inc. and McGregor Door & Hardware LLC.

About ADENTRA

ADENTRA is one of North America's largest distributors of architectural building products to the residential, repair and remodel, and commercial construction markets. The Company operates a network of 82 facilities in the United States and Canada. ADENTRA's common shares are listed on the TSX under the symbol ADEN.

Basis of Presentation

Unless otherwise noted, amounts relating to AccessSMT are in Canadian dollars ("C$") and amounts relating to ADENTRA are in United States dollars ("US$"). U.S. dollar equivalents of Canadian dollar amounts are provided for convenience only, at an exchange rate of US$0.715 per C$1.00, ADENTRA's average exchange rate for the third quarter of 2026.

Financial information relating to AccessSMT in this news release is derived from AccessSMT's audited consolidated financial statements for the year ended December 31, 2025, prepared in accordance with Canadian accounting standards for private enterprises ("ASPE"), and from AccessSMT's unaudited internal management reports, as adjusted by ADENTRA based on its due diligence. This information has not been prepared in accordance with IFRS Accounting Standards, may not be comparable to ADENTRA's financial information, and has not been audited or reviewed by ADENTRA's auditors. Pro forma information is provided for illustrative purposes only and is not necessarily indicative of the results that would have been achieved had the Acquisition been completed on the dates indicated, or of future results.

Non-GAAP and Other Financial Measures

This news release refers to certain non-GAAP and other financial measures and non-GAAP ratios. These measures are not standardized financial measures under IFRS Accounting Standards (in the case of ADENTRA) or ASPE (in the case of AccessSMT) and might not be comparable to similar financial measures disclosed by other issuers.

  • "Adjusted EBITDA", as it relates to ADENTRA, is EBITDA before share-based compensation expense, transaction expenses, and net recovery of trade duties and tariffs, where "EBITDA" is earnings before interest, income taxes, depreciation and amortization. We believe Adjusted EBITDA is a useful supplemental measure for investors, and it is used by management for evaluating our ability to meet debt service requirements and fund organic and inorganic growth, and as an indicator of relative operating performance.
  • "Adjusted EBITDA", as it relates to AccessSMT, is earnings before interest, income taxes, depreciation and amortization, determined in accordance with ASPE and adjusted for non-recurring items and accounting and normalization adjustments identified in ADENTRA's due diligence, including a quality of earnings review. Because AccessSMT reports under ASPE, its Adjusted EBITDA is stated after lease expense and is therefore not directly comparable to ADENTRA's Adjusted EBITDA, which reflects IFRS 16, Leases.
  • "Adjusted EBITDA margin" is Adjusted EBITDA as a percentage of sales or revenue.
  • "Adjusted basic EPS" refers to adjusted basic earnings per share, which is basic earnings per share excluding the after-tax impact of share-based compensation expense, transaction expense, net recovery of trade duties and tariffs, foreign exchange gain (loss), and amortization of intangible assets acquired in connection with an acquisition.
  • "Pro Forma Leverage Ratio" is net bank debt divided by expected Adjusted EBITDA for 2026 after deducting rental payments related to premises. Management uses it to assess financial leverage, capital structure, debt service capacity and financing flexibility.
  • "Contracted backlog" is the remaining value of awarded and contracted work that has not yet been invoiced.

For a reconciliation of ADENTRA's non-GAAP measures and non-GAAP ratios to the most directly comparable measures in its financial statements, please refer to sections 2.0, 4.2 and 4.3 of ADENTRA's management's discussion and analysis for the three and nine months ended September 30, 2026, available under ADENTRA's profile on SEDAR+ at www.sedarplus.ca.

data.title: Zoom Communications Profit Falls, But Revenues Up; Shares Down After-market
data.description:
WASHINGTON (dpa-AFX) - Zoom Communications, Inc. (ZM), a software company, on Monday reported a decline in its third quarter earnings, mainly impacted by one-time gains. The company provided its guidance for the fourth quarter, and also upgraded its estimates for the full year 2027.

Net income decreased to $312.405 million, or $1.05 per share, from $612.873 million, or $2.01 per share, a year ago.

Operating income was $317.736 million, compared to $310.414 million in the previous year.

Gains on strategic investments for the third quarter of 2026 and 2025 were $10.184 million and $406.060 million, respectively.

Revenue for the period was $1.290 billion, up 4.9 percent year-over-year from $1.229 billion.

Third-quarter enterprise revenue was $805.4 million, up 8.6% year over year.

Looking ahead for the fourth quarter, Zoom expects the adjusted income from operations to be between $539.0 million and $544.0 million. On a per-share basis, it is expected to range between $1.55 and $1.57. Revenue for the quarter is estimated at $1.293 billion - $1.298 billion.

For fiscal 2027, adjusted income from operations is seen to range between $2.095 billion and $2.100 billion, up from the earlier estimate of $2.065 - $2.075 billion. Adjusted earnings per share are now revised to $6.24 - $6.25, up from the earlier expectation of $6.08 - $6.12.

Revenue outlook for the full year is upgraded to a range of $5.100 billion - $5.105 billion. The previous outlook was $5.085 billion - $5.095 billion.

In the after-hours activity Monday on the Nasdaq, the company's shares lost 0.96 percent and traded at $85.20.

data.title: US judge approves Getty Images bankruptcy loan over shareholder objections
data.description:
By Dietrich Knauth

A US bankruptcy judge on Monday approved a $143 million bankruptcy loan for Getty Images provided by Koch Equity Development, overruling objections from shareholders who had argued that the loan would allow Getty insiders to shortchange minority investors.

  • US Bankruptcy Judge J. Kate Stickles in Delaware said the loan was the best available financing for Getty's bankruptcy restructuring

  • Objecting shareholders had said the loan would essentially hand the company to the Getty family and Koch Equity Development while leaving other shareholders with nothing

  • Stickles on Friday denied shareholders' request for a court-appointed committee to represent equity holders

  • Getty cited court losses in investor litigation, its $1.46 billion ​in debt, a failed merger with Shutterstock, and increased competition from AI-generated imagery as reasons for its bankruptcy filing in October

  • Getty said affiliates of ​the Getty family and Koch Equity Development, which committed to ​provide up to $533 million in new equity, will own 100% of the company after the bankruptcy restructuring

  • Getty Images expects to complete ​the restructuring by ​year-end

The case is Getty Images Holdings Inc, ​US Bankruptcy Court for the District of Delaware, No. 26-11643

For Getty Images: Brian Schartz of Simpson Thacher & Bartlett

For an ad hoc group of equity holders: Shari Dwoskin and Robert Stark of ​Brown Rudnick

Getty Images plans bankruptcy filing, to go private

Getty Images scraps $3.7 billion merger with Shutterstock over UK scrutiny

Getty Images says investor litigation helped push it to bankruptcy

data.title: UN food agency chief warns wars jeopardize food aid for 7.3 million more people
data.description:
Key points:
  • WFP chief calls for new Black Sea initiative
  • UN agency aims to feed 91 million people in 2027
  • Wars, attacks are raising transport costs, keeping grain from markets

By Andrea Shalal

World Food Programme Executive Director Luke Lindberg warned on Monday that shipping chokepoints linked to wars in the Middle East and Ukraine could raise the agency's costs by $727 million by mid-2027, threatening food aid for 7.3 million more people.

Lindberg, whom US President Donald Trump nominated and the United Nations appointed in September to head the world's largest humanitarian agency, called for new efforts to safeguard humanitarian shipments of Ukrainian and Russian grain through the Black Sea, modeled on a UN-brokered initiative that was in effect from 2022 to 2023.

Lindberg told the UN Security Council that constraints on food exports and farming inputs passing through the Strait of Hormuz, the Bab el-Mandeb Strait and the Black Sea were compounded by climate shocks like El Nino.

"It's an unthinkable scenario, and it could not come at a worse time," said Lindberg, a former US agriculture official, urging diplomats to focus on trying to find rapid solutions to ensure some 10 million tons of Ukrainian and Russian grain that were already in silos reached people in need.

He said 266 million people globally were already suffering from acute hunger and there was a risk of famine in parts of Sudan, South Sudan, and Somalia.

Lindberg told Reuters in an interview that it was critical to resolve the situation in the Black Sea, one of the world's breadbasket regions whose grains were vital to countries like Somalia and Yemen, which imports 90% of its food.

He urged diplomats to work on a humanitarian corridor similar to the Black Sea Grain Initiative, a UN-brokered deal agreed in ​July 2022 ​that allowed ⁠the safe export of nearly 33 million metric tons of ​Ukrainian grain. Russia withdrew from the agreement in 2023, complaining that its own ⁠food ​and fertilizer exports faced ​serious obstacles.

'UNTENABLE'

Lindberg told Reuters that any revived agreement would have to cover both Russian and Ukrainian exports to win agreement.

"It's untenable to have full grain silos in Ukraine and Poland and the region, and then you have empty stomachs in other parts of the world ... If a diplomatic solution can be reached, we stand ready to move grain from both Russia and Ukraine," he said.

The WFP head added Black Sea food shipments were down sharply this year, with 63% fewer wheat and maize vessels moving through the Bosphorus as of mid-October than at the same point in 2025. Over 300 attacks had been recorded and at least 40 crew members had been killed, he said.

That meant some 10 million tons of Russian and Ukrainian wheat might not reach global markets this year — enough to feed 44 million people, he said.

The food price index of the UN's Food and Agriculture Organization had hit a near four-year high this September, wheat prices were up almost 10% from January, and higher energy and transport costs had increased grocery prices, especially in import-dependent and food-insecure countries, Lindberg said.

Food yields will likely also be lower next season, given constraints in global fertilizer supplies, of which 30% flow through the Strait of Hormuz, he added.

The wars were taking a direct toll on WFP's humanitarian operations and sharply increasing its costs, he said. The WFP has already lowered its target to provide food assistance to 91 million people in 2027 from 110 million people this year, but higher costs could drive that number even lower, he said.

The agency's total costs last year were nearly $12.2 billion, so $727 million in additional costs by mid-2027 would mark an increase of nearly 6%. That number could rise further unless current conditions changed, the agency said.

data.title: Meta pauses Class C share issuance amid shareholder lawsuit
data.description:
Meta Platforms said on Monday it will not issue its planned Class C shares while it faces shareholder litigation challenging the company's proposed recapitalization, delaying a share sale program intended to help fund its artificial intelligence investments.

  • The social media giant agreed not to issue the shares during the pre-trial and trial proceedings in the lawsuit brought by shareholders in Delaware's Court of Chancery. The trial is scheduled to begin on April 19, 2027

  • The shareholder litigation challenges Meta's plan to create a new class of non-voting Class C common stock in January 2027

  • The structure would effectively result in a two-for-one split and is designed to give Meta flexibility to fund acquisitions and retain top talent while maintaining CEO Mark Zuckerberg's voting control

  • The delay also affects Meta's planned $60 billion at-the-market stock sale program, which is not expected to begin until the Class C shares start trading

  • The company has been investing heavily in advanced chips and data centers as it steps up competition with AI leaders OpenAI and Anthropic, while positioning itself at the forefront of the emerging consumer AI agent race
